# Position Control of a Micro Servo Motor (SG90) Using Arduino Uno

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

# Aim

To interface an SG90 servo motor with an Arduino Uno development board and write an embedded C/C++ program to control its angular displacement from 0° to 180° and back using Pulse Width Modulation (PWM).

## Component

![][image1]
![imagere1](componentservo.png)
### &nbsp;Working

A servo motor operates as a **closed-loop negative feedback servomechanism** composed of four elements: a miniature DC motor, a reduction gear train, a position-sensing potentiometer coupled to the output shaft, and an internal error-detection amplifier.

1. **Error Detection:** The internal circuitry continuously compares the voltage from the feedback potentiometer with the reference voltage generated by the incoming PWM signal.  
2. **Torque Generation:** An error amplifier calculates the difference between current position and target position. It drives the DC motor forward or reverse until the feedback voltage matches the reference setpoint, reducing angular error to zero.  
3. **PWM Modulation Standard:**  
   * **Signal Period:** $20\\text{ ms}$ ($50\\text{ Hz}$ frame rate).  
   * **Pulse Width:**  
     * 1.0 ms 0 degree (Minimum position)  
     * 1.5 ms  90 degree (Neutral position)  
     * 2.0 ms 180 degree (Maximum position)

The Arduino \<Servo.h\> library utilizes the microcontroller's internal 16-bit hardware timer (Timer 1\) to generate non-blocking, jitter-free control pulses.

CODE

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

/\*

&nbsp;\* Experiment: Sweep Control of Servo Motor

&nbsp;\* Board: Arduino Uno (ATmega328P)

&nbsp;\*/

&nbsp;

\#include \<Servo.h\>

&nbsp;

Servo myServo;  // Instantiate servo object

&nbsp;

const int servoPin \= 9;  // Hardware PWM pin assigned to servo signal line

int angle \= 0;           // Variable to track current angular position

&nbsp;

void setup() {

&nbsp;&nbsp;myServo.attach(servoPin);  // Bind signal generation to digital pin 9

}

&nbsp;

void loop() {

&nbsp;&nbsp;// Sweep forward from 0 degrees to 180 degrees

&nbsp;&nbsp;for (angle \= 0; angle \<= 180; angle \+= 1\) {

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;myServo.write(angle);

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delay(15);  // Dwell time allowing rotor to track the command angle

&nbsp;&nbsp;}

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;// Sweep backward from 180 degrees to 0 degrees

&nbsp;&nbsp;for (angle \= 180; angle \>= 0; angle \-= 1\) {

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;myServo.write(angle);

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;delay(15);

&nbsp;&nbsp;}

}

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Applications

&nbsp;

* **Robotics:** Articulated joints in robotic arms, grippers, and bipedal/hexapod walking platforms.  
* **Aeromodelling & Avionics:** Primary flight control surfaces (ailerons, elevators, rudders) in RC aircraft and UAVs.  
* **Optics & Vision Systems:** Pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) camera mounts and two-axis gimbal stabilization platforms.  
* **Mechatronics & Automation:** Automated sorting gates, smart door locking mechanisms, and fluid valve throttling.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Result

&nbsp;

The interfacing of the SG90 micro servo motor with the Arduino Uno was implemented and verified. The servo successfully achieved smooth, bi-directional angular displacement across its full dynamic range from $0^\\circ$ to $180^\\circ$ and returned to $0^\\circ$ in continuous succession with uniform angular velocity and stable positioning.
